sections.content: How many people are "special and additional needs education teaching professionals"?

31,435 people

were counted on the census as "special and additional needs education teaching professionals" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Special and additional needs education teaching professionals organise and provide instruction at a variety of different levels to children who have emotional, behavioural or learning difficulties or physical disabilities.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "special and additional needs education teaching professionals" there were more women than men (85.8% compared with 14.2%).

This means "special and additional needs education teaching professionals" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "teaching and other educational professionals".

Men made up 14.2% and women made up 85.8% of "special and additional needs education teaching professionals"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "special and additional needs education teaching professionals" included:

  • health care practice managers
  • human resources administrative occupations
  • complementary health associate professionals

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 45 to 49 years. Of the whole working population 11% were aged 45 to 49 years. For people working as "special and additional needs education teaching professionals", 14.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "special and additional needs education teaching professionals" was 16 to 19 years.

The percentage of men and women who are "special and additional needs education teaching professionals" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "special and additional needs education teaching professionals", 12.4% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (69.4% compared with 30.6%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (95.6%) than self-employed (4.4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
